page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-288-metal is a bare-metal server configured with 288 vCPUs across 144 physical cores, utilizing the x86_64 Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor running at 4.2 GHz. It features 2232 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory operating at 6 GHz, providing 7.75 GB of RAM per core. The processor includes a 504 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for accelerated matrix mathematics. This instance does not include local storage or onboard GPUs.

In benchmark testing, the server demonstrates top-tier multi-core performance, achieving a stress-ng multi-core score of 313,057.86 and a PassMark CPU score of 179,028.27. Its memory subsystem delivers exceptional throughput, with read-only large block memory bandwidth reaching 1090.07 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 412.54 GB/sec. Database and in-memory operations are highly efficient, as evidenced by a Redis SET throughput of 423.02 million operations per second and a top-tier PassMark database operations score. However, single-core performance is more moderate, with stress-ng single-core results falling into the average tier.

From a resource density perspective, this bare-metal configuration offers high cost efficiency for workloads requiring massive parallel compute and memory capacity without virtualization overhead. The absence of local NVMe storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, which may introduce latency tradeoffs for disk-heavy applications. The server is highly suited for large-scale in-memory databases, high-throughput web serving, heavy multi-threaded compilation, and memory-intensive enterprise workloads. It also supports moderate LLM prompt processing workloads utilizing its AMX instruction set, though text generation speeds for smaller models are relatively low.
